newsitem.title: FRANCE: Oman LNG project set for speedy start.
newsitem.headline: Oman LNG project set for speedy start.

text.p: The signing earlier this month of financing and construction contracts has put the Oman liquefied natural gas (LNG) project on course for a speedy start-up in 2000, Tony Hanna, general manager and chief executive of Oman LNG, said.
Hanna told a conference that the LNG project, Oman's largest industrial endeavour, was the fastest such operation ever put together.
"Timing in getting an LNG project off the ground is crucial. Oman LNG was designed with the vision of a supply-demand gap developing in 2000 and we look forward to satisfying some of that demand."
From the first major discovery to signing of the first sale and purchase contract had taken five years, and first delivery would follow nine years after discovery of gas, he said.

Oman LNG is designed to produce 6.6 million tonnes a year of which 6.2 million tonnes will be shipped to the Far East. A supply agreement with the Omani government was signed on October 22 and the following day Oman LNG signed a contract with Korea Gas Corp to delivery 4.1 million tonnes a year from 2000.
The company also signed a preliminary agreement with Thailand's PTT in August to supply up to 2.2 million tonnes a year form 2003.

Oman LNG was created to handle the downstream of the export project, consisting of liquefaction, transport and sales. The shareholders are the government of Oman 51 percent, Shell 30 percent, Total SA 5.54 percent. Partex, Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Itochu and a yet-to-be-formed Korean company all have small holdings.
A separate company uniting the government, Shell, Total and Partex is responsible for the upstream side.
